sources.entry: diffusers - Pre-trained diffusion models for generating and editing images, audio, and video.

summary.one_liner: Hugging Face's Python library of pretrained diffusion pipelines, noise schedulers, and models for generating and editing images, audio, and 3D molecular structures.
summary.what_it_does: Provides ready-to-run diffusion pipelines that load pretrained checkpoints from the Hugging Face Hub with a few lines of code (e.g., DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained for text-to-image). It offers interchangeable noise schedulers that trade off diffusion speed against output quality. It also exposes pretrained models such as UNet2DModel as building blocks to combine with schedulers into custom end-to-end diffusion systems. The README lists tasks including unconditional image generation, text-to-image, ControlNet and InstructPix2Pix image-to-image, inpainting, image variation, and super resolution. It also states support for training diffusion models, with guides in the documentation.
use_cases: build a custom diffusion model from components
run Stable Diffusion locally in Python
how_to_run: from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline; pipeline = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained("stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5", dtype=torch.float16)
pipeline("An image of a squirrel in Picasso style").images[0]
notable: Three core components: pipelines, interchangeable noise schedulers, and pretrained models usable as building blocks
Access to 30,000+ pretrained checkpoints on the Hugging Face Hub, per the README
Modular Diffusers section for building systems from pipeline components
Documentation covers optimization guides for speed and memory use
Project conventions in a .ai/ directory for AI coding agents, installable as a plugin or skill
caveats: README says the library favors usability over performance, so it is not positioned as the fastest option
Running models on GPU is shown with CUDA; the README points to a separate guide for Apple Silicon rather than detailing it
Many pipelines require downloading large pretrained checkpoints from the Hub
